instruction:
Please run the General Lake Model to simulate the vertical water temperature for Lake Mendota. The RMSE between the observation and the simulation should be smaller than 2 degrees Celsius.

The data that you may use includes:
1. Meteorological and hydrological forcing data in `/root/bcs/`
2. Field water temperature observations data in `/root/field_temp_oxy.csv`
3. GLM configuration file in `/root/glm3.nml`.

You should generate the simulation output from 2009-01-01 to 2015-12-30 at `/root/output/output.nc`.
In addition, I will check that GLM can run successfully with the parameters you used (final parameters are saved in `/root/glm3.nml`).

items.requirement: Run the General Lake Model (GLM) to produce a vertical water temperature simulation for Lake Mendota, and the model must execute successfully.
items.source_quote: Please run the General Lake Model to simulate the vertical water temperature for Lake Mendota.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by running `glm` in /root and confirming the process exits with return code 0.

items.requirement: Achieve a root-mean-square error (RMSE) between simulated and observed water temperatures that is smaller than 2.0 degrees Celsius.
items.source_quote: The RMSE between the observation and the simulation should be smaller than 2 degrees Celsius.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by matching simulated temperatures from output.nc to observations in field_temp_oxy.csv on identical datetime/depth pairs and confirming the computed RMSE is below 2.0C.

items.requirement: Produce the simulation output as a NetCDF file located at /root/output/output.nc.
items.source_quote: You should generate the simulation output from 2009-01-01 to 2015-12-30 at `/root/output/output.nc`.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by checking that the file /root/output/output.nc exists on disk.

items.requirement: The simulation output must cover the full requested time span, from 2009-01-01 through 2015-12-30.
items.source_quote: You should generate the simulation output from 2009-01-01 to 2015-12-30 at `/root/output/output.nc`.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by reading the 'time' variable in output.nc, converting it to dates using the 2009-01-01 12:00:00 reference start, and confirming the covered range spans from approximately 2009-01-01 to 2015-12-30.
items.notes: The verifier's RMSE test only checks overlap with observation dates, so full-range coverage is not directly asserted by the given test code.

items.requirement: Save the final calibrated parameter values back into /root/glm3.nml so that GLM can be re-run standalone (without extra agent intervention) to reproduce the reported results.
items.source_quote: I will check that GLM can run successfully with the parameters you used (final parameters are saved in `/root/glm3.nml`).
items.verification: A grader can verify this by running `glm` from /root (which reads glm3.nml from the working directory by default) with no other configuration changes and confirming it completes successfully, indicating the final parameters are persisted in that file.
